chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a basin in which there are images, or a jug, or a large bowl in which there are images or silver, he said: “Wudu (ablution) is not performed from it, nor in it.”
And about a man, when he trims his nails with iron, or takes from his hair, or shaves the back of his neck, he said: “Then it is upon him to wipe it with water before he performs salat (prayer).”
He was asked: if he performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that with water? He said: “He wipes with water and repeats the salat (prayer), because iron is najas (ritually impure).”
And he said: “Indeed, iron is the attire of the people of the Fire, and gold is the attire of the people of Paradise.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains in his statement عليه السلام, “He was asked: if he performed salat (prayer) and did not wipe any of that,” it is possible that the one asked was the narrator, not Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. If there is no explicit wording identifying the one asked, we interpret it according to what we have stated, because touching iron is not something that necessitates repeating the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الْحَدِيدَ: iron, mentioned here in relation to grooming tools
key_terms.تَمَاثِيلُ: figures or images depicted on the vessel
key_terms.لَا يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is not to be performed
key_terms.لِبَاسُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ: the attire of the people of the Fire
key_terms.لِبَاسُ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: the attire of the people of Paradise

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about performing wudu (ablution) from decorated vessels and about washing after using iron before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to wudu (ablution), vessels containing images or silver, and washing after contact with iron during grooming before salat (prayer). It also includes Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s clarification that the wording about repeating the prayer may refer to the narrator’s statement rather than a direct statement of the Imam عليه السلام, since mere contact with iron does not require repeating salat (prayer).
